insights.headline: Gold whipsaws around $4,150 as Fed-hike bets swing with oil and the dollar; Indian premiums return ahead of Diwali
insights.summary: Spot gold swung between $4,184 and below $4,150 on Monday as softer oil first cooled, then a rebounding dollar revived, Fed rate-hike bets; traders see ~16% odds of an October hike but near-92% for December. Silver bounced from its $55.56 low to hold the $56-$57 zone, while a firm rupee kept domestic moves muted. Indian dealers charged up to $7/oz premiums - the first in over three months - as festive and wedding demand picked up, even as September gold imports fell to $1.8B from $9.6B YoY. The RBI fixed the SGB 2020-21 Series VII redemption at Rs 14,614/unit for Oct 19.
points: Spot gold touched $4,184 in Asia, then slipped below $4,150 as the dollar rebounded; $4,201 is the breakout test, $4,000-$4,020 the support below.
Fed pricing: ~16% chance of an October hike, near-92% for December; Warsh's remarks cooled October bets.
India: dealers charge up to $7/oz premium - first in 3+ months - on festive and wedding demand; Sept imports fell to $1.8B from $9.6B YoY.
Silver holds $56-$57 after bouncing from $55.56; a break below $56 targets $51-$52, above $57 opens $60.
RBI set SGB 2020-21 Series VII early redemption at Rs 14,614/unit for Oct 19; online subscribers book ~192% gains.

trending.title: Fed-hike bets are the market's steering wheel
trending.summary: Gold's arc from $4,184 to below $4,150 tracks oil and the dollar, but the deeper story is rate pricing: ~16% for October, near-92% for December. Rallies die at resistance until that pricing shifts.

trending.title: India's premium flip signals real festive demand
trending.summary: Dealers flipped from $6 discounts to $7 premiums - the first premium in three months - as wedding and festive buying returned despite September imports falling ~80% YoY.

trending.title: Silver bounces but stays the weaker metal
trending.summary: Silver reclaimed the $56-$57 band off its $55.56 low, yet sellers stay in control below the $57.86 trendline. Hindustan Zinc's 20% output jump shows miners cheering as investors stay wary.

trending.title: Domestic prices dance to the rupee's tune
trending.summary: A firm rupee - up a seventh straight session - pushed spot gold lower even as global futures held, showing why Indian buyers track the currency as closely as COMEX.

items.title: Gold eyes $4,201 breakout as oil dip cools Fed bets; Indian dealers flip to $7/oz premiums
items.summary: Gold consolidated near $4,184 with $4,201 as a breakout test, as softer oil cooled October Fed-hike odds to ~16%; traders price a near-92% chance of a December hike. Indian dealers flipped to up to $7/oz premiums - the first in over three months - on festive and wedding demand, even as September imports fell to $1.8B from $9.6B YoY. Silver held $57.60, capped by $57.86 trendline resistance.

items.title: Gold slips back below $4,150 as dollar rebounds; silver holds $56-$57 support
items.summary: Gold slipped back below $4,150 as a rebounding dollar and firmer yields revived rate pressure; traders see only ~17% odds of an October hike but expect hikes in December and January. A sustained break below $4,150 opens $4,000-$4,020 support, with resistance at $4,160-$4,180. Silver held the $56-$57 band as the gold-silver ratio pulled below 72.5; platinum gained despite higher yields.

items.title: Gold climbs Rs 400 to Rs 1.5 lakh per 10 gm as festive buying elevates demand
items.summary: Delhi gold rose Rs 400 to Rs 1,50,300 per 10 grams, inclusive of taxes, on Monday as festive demand picked up ahead of Dussehra; silver held steady at Rs 2.15 lakh per kg. HDFC Securities' Saumil Gandhi said domestic gold traded at a premium last week for the first time in three months and expects retail demand to build toward Diwali. Bullion markets shut Tuesday for Dussehra.

items.title: Gold edges higher as traders ease rate-hike bets on Warsh speech
items.summary: Spot gold climbed toward $4,190 after Fed Chair Kevin Warsh's remarks were read as favoring a pause at the Oct 27-28 meeting, with traders cutting the implied chance of an October hike to below one-in-six. A hot inflation print last week had lifted hike bets and the dollar; Warsh's comments halted the dollar's gains. Silver rose about 1.5% to $57.80.

items.title: Spot gold slightly down on firm rupee; markets see no Fed rate hike in Oct
items.summary: Spot gold in India's major markets slipped Rs 20 to Rs 1,46,406 per 10 grams as the rupee rose for a seventh straight session, cheapening dollar-denominated metal. But December MCX futures added 0.2% to Rs 1,48,221 and COMEX futures held near $4,197.80 as traders priced in a Fed hold in October after Warsh's remarks, with softer crude adding support.

items.title: RBI sets SGB 2020-21 Series VII redemption at Rs 14,614 for October 19
items.summary: The RBI has fixed October 19, 2026 as the premature redemption date for Sovereign Gold Bond 2020-21 Series VII at Rs 14,614 per gram, based on IBJA's average closing prices of October 14-16. Online subscribers gain 192.22% and offline buyers 189.33% in capital gains, alongside 2.5% annual interest; holders must route requests through their receiving offices within the notification window.

items.title: Hindustan Zinc Q2 profit more than doubles on higher metal prices; silver output up 20%
items.summary: Hindustan Zinc's consolidated net profit more than doubled to Rs 6,412 crore in Q2 FY27 as higher metal prices and record output lifted revenue 76.5% to Rs 15,093 crore, margin widening to 42%. Silver production rose 20% to 173 tonnes and silver sales revenue more than doubled, driving about 45% of profitability; Jefferies said firmer silver prices improved the profit outlook.

items.title: IBJA's Surendra Mehta sees gold rallying 10-12% to $4,700 by November 30
items.summary: IBJA national secretary Surendra Mehta told ET Now Swadesh he expects gold to rally 10-12% by November 30, potentially reaching $4,700 an ounce, as bond yields ease below 5.1% and crude stabilises near $105. He put the downside at 4-5% (a move toward $3,850 not ruled out) and said India's festive season could support prices, barring fresh geopolitical escalation.

items.title: Gold slips, silver gains as oil retreats and Fed-pause expectations hold - Kitco AM Report
items.summary: Kitco's morning note has spot gold slightly lower at $4,159.70 (-0.11%) and spot silver higher at $57.30 (+0.77%) in early US trading, as retreating oil prices and lower Treasury yields supported metals while sticky inflation and expectations of further Fed tightening capped buying. A later afternoon note put spot near $4,150, little changed as investors awaited the Oct 27-28 Fed meeting.

items.title: Gold on Dhanteras: celebrate the ritual, rethink the investment
items.summary: A Mint column argues Dhanteras gold buying is a cherished tradition that should not be mistaken for investing: most purchases are jewellery with making charges that vanish on resale, or coins sitting in rented lockers. Buying an asset on a set date because it is auspicious is consumption, not a financial plan - enjoy the ritual, but judge the purchase on its merits.

items.title: Central Banks Are Buying Gold - So Why Is the Yellow Metal Still Under Pressure?
items.summary: Fawad Razaqzada argues gold's bearish trend remains intact: elevated oil, 10-year Treasury yields above 5.05% and sticky inflation keep tightening bets alive, capping rallies. He flags $4,100 as the line to watch - a break could expose $4,000 - with resistance at $4,223-$4,260. Until that pressure eases, recoveries face an uphill struggle and the burden of proof is on the bulls.

items.title: Gold and silver head for volatile week amid crude oil spike, West Asia worries
items.summary: PTI reports MCX December gold fell Rs 3,581 (-2.4%) last week to Rs 1.47 lakh/10g, and silver Rs 14,568 (-6.4%) to Rs 2.11 lakh/kg. The rupee's jump to 94.8 from ~96.8 in five sessions on RBI intervention cut import costs, dragging domestic prices down ~5x the global fall. Analysts expect a capped, choppy week: Brent near $110, West Asia tensions, and Tuesday's Dussehra morning closure.
